reason: A saved visibility/appearance state is not a model configuration or a single show/hide command. Paired display panes express switching one saved presentation to another.
Creates an independently named model configuration. The configuration sheet and add mark distinguish it from viewing the existing configuration table.
Marks configuration persistence behavior rather than immediately rebuilding or saving. A save container with a rebuild loop expresses that combined command.
Creates a traversable camera route, not an orbit, camera sensor or robot path. The scene boundaries, person and route communicate a walk-through.
Contact/crevice shading is distinct from cast shadows and executing a renderer. The glyph places a dark contact band where a solid approaches a corner.
Browsable visual swatches are not a physical material assignment. A swatch reference book denotes choosing reusable appearances.
Assigns a visible finish rather than physical constitutive properties. A brush applying appearance to a face communicates the actual operation.
Looking through a model camera differs from a screenshot or configuring a sensor. The camera/frustum glyph represents a viewing volume.
Retains visible geometry with reduced opacity, unlike hide/show. Overlapping see-through panels express transparency; assembly and part scope aliases reuse it.
Checks external read-only document changes, not just locking or reloading. A document and lock-inspection lens denote this check.
Restores the model plus undo history checkpoint, not one Undo step or a history active marker. The stored checkpoint returns into the history line.
Captures model and undo-history state rather than writing the ordinary document file. A history node enters a checkpoint store.
Trials a candidate configuration without activating it. A provisional wireframe with a viewing eye avoids implying parameter editing.
Conditional model configuration logic is not the existing parameter table. A decision diamond with two branches expresses the rule family.
Opening diagnostic traces is an action, not an error status. A report page with a failure trace represents this navigation.
Shows reference topology and downstream users, not chronological history or creating a link. Connected graph nodes represent dependencies.
Checks design-document requirements and properties; analysis model-precheck is a different study-validation operation. A document checklist metaphor represents this family.
Creates/learns reusable checking requirements rather than running a check. A rule sheet and editing pencil distinguish rule authoring.
Curated reusable local resources have a browsing-library meaning beyond opening a file or a folder object. Compartmentalized shelves show reusable resource types.
Evaluates direction-dependent stiffness rather than assigning material axes or plotting a generic simulation result. A directional polar lobe expresses anisotropic modulus.
One mixed wireframe/shaded solid represents the display-style chooser. Wireframe, HLR/HLV, shaded and cartoon options are aliases, not separate drawings.
A standalone expression calculator does not create/edit model parameters or derived analysis fields. Calculator geometry represents evaluating an expression.

Transfers formatting rather than duplicating content or assigning model appearance. A paint roller is the independent format-transfer metaphor.
Environmental light is distinct from a flat background or render execution. A sky dome and bright source communicate panoramic illumination.
Equal-axis viewing direction is not the orthographic projection toggle. A balanced cube and three axes show the isometric orientation.
Uses local magnification for picking, not zooming to an existing selection. A pointer inside a lens makes that distinction visible.
Review freehand markup differs from dimension/leader annotation and source-model editing. A review cloud and pencil represent the independent operation.
Material definitions are created and browsed independently of assigning them. A material specimen in a reference book expresses the library.
Constitutive material consistency checks differ from assignment, acceptance or a warning state. A physical specimen and check represent validation.
Applies a saved camera state rather than changing projection. A bookmarked image with an apply arrow expresses restoring a named view.
Creates another UI view of an existing document, not a new file. Layered windows with add operation express the difference.
Returns in camera history without undoing geometry edits. A view frame and return arrow keep this distinct from model Undo.
Adjusts a finished image or lens effects rather than geometry or render dispatch. A lens and sparkle express optical/creative finishing.
Browses mixed render assets, not just appearance swatches. Stacked scene-resource cards express that wider library family.
Configures emitters and rigs rather than material properties or executing a render. A supported spotlight and rays express illumination setup.
Validates render requests before dispatch, unlike Run or generic warning. A scene card and validation check represent the preflight action.
Configures render-only ground/backdrop surfaces, not CAD solids. A studio cyclorama and grounded object express the stage.
Moves a hierarchy item to an explicit position, unlike field-based sorting or moving model geometry. A branch list and insertion direction express structural reordering.
Rotates about the viewing axis, unlike the existing orbit-around-model command. A tilted viewport and opposing roll arrows express camera roll.
Selects entities using criteria rather than filtering the displayed list. A funnel and pointer express semantic selection; all listed criteria share this glyph.
Starts a region selection over geometry rather than directly picking the underlying face. A window starting on a solid and pointer represent this interaction.
Selects through assembly relations, not defining a joint. A shared axis, component pair and pointer express relation-based selection.

Turns look direction from a fixed position, unlike orbiting the model. A fixed camera base, viewing rays and turn arc express this action.
Shortens presentation without sectioning/splitting the source model. Two aligned ends and break lines express an interrupted view.
Aligns the camera normal to selected geometry rather than projection or general orbit. A selected plane and its normal vector express the direction.
Controls graphic fidelity/performance rather than generic application preferences. Stepped and smooth silhouettes in one viewport express quality choices.
A 3D selection volume differs from 2D window/crossing/lasso selection. A dashed volume containing objects expresses spatial inclusion.
Changes disconnected document workflow, unlike unlinking an object reference. A disconnected cloud/local-store composition expresses offline operation.
Arranges workspace panels and tiled windows, not fullscreen or generic settings. Divided window regions express this family of layout choices.
